newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Absa mulling 500 mln rand tier-two issue.
newsitem.headline: Absa mulling 500 mln rand tier-two issue.

text.p: Amalgamated Banks of South Africa Ltd (Absa) said on Thursday it was mulling the issue of 500 million rand worth of secondary capital by September to boost its capital adequacy ratio above nine percent.
The group earlier announced a $110 million equity offer.

"Only other thing local is we might supplement our surplus capital by probably secondary, or tier two, capital in the local market to put it (the capital adequacy ratio) back over nine percent," group executive director Alwyn Noeth told Reuters.
He said the a domestic issue of non-convertible debentures with maturities of between five and 10 years was the most likely option.
"There's no way we're going to do a rights issue or further issue of tier one capital in the near future," he added.
The bank's total capital was 7.4 billion rand at March 31 compared with a statutory requirement of 6.9 billion.
